newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Frankfurt, Milan shares hit peaks, London dull.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Frankfurt, Milan shares hit peaks, London dull.

text.p: Stocks in Frankfurt and Milan stormed to closing peaks on Wednesday helped by the stronger dollar but London ended with only modest gains, preoccupied with worries over higher interest rates.
On currency markets, the dollar and sterling edged to near multi-year records against the mark, which was weakened by speculation about a broad-based start to European monetary union.
In precious metals, gold, which has suffered from recent heavy selling, strengthened at the close of trade after hitting a near 12-year low at the morning fix.

The German and Italian bourses were the best performers of the day, with Frankfurt making its seventh consecutive closing record. Paris also made a powerful finish but London, Europe's biggest stock exchange, ended only just in the plus column.

Frankfurt's cracking pace did not let up. The DAX index surged 1.25 percent to yet another closing record at 4,055.86 points, underpinned by the rising dollar, which boosts prospects for German exporters.
"There seems to be nothing around to brake us at the moment," said a Frankfurt trader.

"The dollar is giving us a push, Bunds(government bonds) are helping, the U.S. is helping and there are no negative corporate stories out there. I don't see any justification for pulling out, even at these highs," the trader said.

In Milan, stocks and bonds soared to record highs as financial markets were seized by a growing conviction that Italy would be a founder member of European economic and monetary union (EMU), planned for launch in 1999.
"Money is pouring in and it looks like we could see a substantial rerating of Italy," said an equities specialist with a foreign finance house in Milan.
The bourse was swept along by a torrent of money from foreign and domestic investors seeking rich pickings as a programme of sell-offs of state assets gathers pace.
The all-share Mibtel index, which tracks all stocks traded on the exchange, hit 13,943 points-- its highest level ever. It ended up 0.88 percent at 13,895, a record close.

The Italian government has made swift progress in restoring order to state accounts and bringing down inflation -- key requirements for EMU membership -- just as France and Germany have run into trouble containing their public sector deficits.
The Paris bourse finished ahead 0.7 percent, losing some early gains with investors perhaps disappointed by an unsteady start on Wall Street after another record close in New York on Tuesday.

New York's recent strength has been behind much of the progress on European bourses. Tuesday's close was the 30th record finish this year for the world's most widely watched stock index but the Dow Jones industrials were down by 0.5 percent at the European close on Wednesday.

London's advance was more modest, with investors distracted by a two-day Bank of England meeting on interest rates starting on Wednesday but with no decision expected until Thursday. Many analysts were predicting an increase of at least 25 basis points to curb inflationary pressures.
The blue-chip FTSE index started trade down about 0.5 percent but managed to claw back the early losses to show a gain of 3.9 points at 4,762.4 at the close.

In currencies, the dollar and the British pound prospered at the expense of the mark, suffering from the talk about a broad-based start to European monetary union making for a soft euro and a perceived Bundesbank ambivalence to its fall.

The dollar touched 1.7650 marks, its highest level since February 1994, before easing to 1.7612 near the close of European trade. The German currency has been hurt by a subdued economic outlook for the country after Bonn reported a rise of 11,000 in unemployment for June.
Sterling slipped back slightly to 2.9676 marks after hitting a six-year high of 2.9760 ahead of the expected rise in UK interest rates on Thursday.
"To some extent this has become a weak-mark story and in the absence of anything new the market's been playing that game," said Adrian Schmidt, economist at Chase Investment Bank.
On bullion markets, gold shot up in late trading to close at $319.75 after a morning fix of $315.75, its lowest since December 11, 1985.

Gold prices have collapsed since the Reserve Bank of Australia last Thursday said it had sold 167 tonnes of gold from its reserves over the past six months. This triggered heavy selling on fears other banks might follow the example.
CURRENCIES
The dollar was at 112.97 yen and 1.7612 marks compared with 112.57 and 1.7594 in late European trade on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index closed up 3.9 points at 4,762.4.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended up 49.46 points at 4,055.86.
PARIS - The CAC-40 finished up 20.75 points at 2,950.56.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $319.75 per ounce, compared to Tuesday's close of $321.95. Silver was at $4.34, down two cents.
